requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 ICMP redirects on node1.
requirements.summary: The executor installed a root-owned sysctl configuration setting all, default, and wildcard interface acceptance to 0. Live values were 0 on every current scope before reboot and remained 0 after a confirmed reboot, directly demonstrating persistence.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 source-routed packets on node1.
requirements.summary: The persistent sysctl configuration covers all, default, and wildcard interface scopes. All observed live interface values were 0 before and after the confirmed reboot, including the previously enabled default, enp1s0, and loopback scopes.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use tooling compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 24.04 and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were identical before and after the work. The implementation used the platform's existing sysctl and systemd-sysctl facilities, and the final package-health observation remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Both IPv4 protections were applied across global, default, and current interface scopes and remained active after reboot. The OS release and kernel were retained. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete and coherent: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovery of system health, networking, persistent configuration, and live hardened values.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The sysctl file creation, permission setting, and live application in cmd-c98ec2cdac504790 directly implemented the requested hardening. The scheduled reboot in cmd-c85b5c41c64647be was required by the provider-wide restart protocol and also verified persistence; its transient timer did not survive the reboot. The intervening failed commands were read-only recovery probes whose connection resets are consistent with the reboot. Afterward there were no failed services, package damage, abandoned temporary artifacts, or material unsafe socket changes; observed temporary-file and process-ID differences were normal reboot regeneration.
